blocks.text: 143 Musaph for the New Year 143

Lord with a Shofar sound’. And it is said: ‘with trumpets and the Shofar sound cry out before the King, the Lord’. And it was said: ‘Blow the Shofar on the new moon, when the moon is covered, on the day of our festival, for it is a statute for Israel, a judgment for the God of Jacob’. And it was said: ‘Halleluyah, praise God for His holiness, praise Him for the strong firmament. Praise Him for His mighty deeds, praise Him for the abundance of His greatness. Praise Him with the Shofar blast, praise Him with zither and the harp. Praise Him with timbrel and dance, praise Him with string instruments and flutes, praise Him with the clash of cymbals, praise Him with the ring of cymbals. Let all with breath praise the Lord, Halleluyah. And through Thy servants the prophets it is written saying: ‘all inhabitants of the world and dwellers on earth, when the banner is raised on the mountain shall you see and when the Shofar is blown shall you hear’. And it was said: ‘And on that day the great Shofar will be blown and the wanderers in the land of Assyria and the banished in the land of Egypt shall come and prostrate themselves to the Lord on the holy mountain in Jerusalem’. And it was said: ‘And the Lord will appear to them and His arrow shall go forth like lightning and the Lord God will blow the Shofar and He will walk in the whirlwinds of the south. The Lord of Hosts will protect them’. So mayest Thou protect Thy people Israel with Thy peace.
uncertainties: The print has no closing quote after 'Halleluyah.' I kept it as printed; see source_sic_corr. The line-end hyphen in 'instru-ments' is joined back as 'instruments'.

blocks.text: 144 Musaph for the New Year 144

Our God and God of our fathers, blow the great Shofar for our freedom and raise a banner for the gathering of our exiles and bring near our dispersed ones from the corners of the earth and bring us to Zion Thy city in mirth and to Jerusalem Thy sanctuary in eternal joy and there we will perform before Thee our sacrificial obligations according to the commandment given to us in Thy Torah through Thy servant Moses from the mouth of Thy glory as it is said: ‘and on the day of your rejoicing and on your festivals and on your new moons, you shall blow trumpets over your whole-offerings and over the sacrifices of your peace-offerings and they shall be a reminder on your behalf before your God, I am the Lord your God’. For Thou dost hear the sound of the Shofar and listen to Teruah and there is none like Thee. Blessed art Thou, O Lord, who hearest the Teruah sound of His people Israel in compassion.
uncertainties: The Hebrew cue א״וא before the first word is excluded as a linkage cue.

blocks.text: The Shofar is blown (but not on the Sabbath).
uncertainties: Printed in italics.

blocks.text: On this day the world was completed. On this day He brings to judgment all the world’s creatures, either like children or like slaves. If like children, then have mercy upon us as a father has mercy on children. If like slaves, then our eyes are lifted to Thee until Thou wilt be gracious to us and make our verdict shine forth like light, O Awe-inspiring and Holy One.
uncertainties: The source hyphenates 'chil-dren' at a line break; joined here. The cue היום is excluded.

blocks.text: May the utterance of our lips be pleasing before Thee, O lofty and exalted God, who understands and listens, pays heed and hearkens to the sound of (the memory of) our Tekioth. Mayest Thou accept with compassion and favour the order of our Shofaroth.
uncertainties: The cue ארשת is excluded.

blocks.text: Take delight, O Lord our God, in Thy people Israel and in their prayer and restore the service to the sanctuary of Thy House and accept with love and favour the fire offerings of Israel and their prayer, and may the service of Thy people Israel be a perpetual delight.
uncertainties: The cue רצה is excluded.

blocks.text: מוֹדִים אֲנַחְנוּ לָךְ שָׁאַתָּה הוּא יְיָ אֱלֹהֵינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵינוּ לְעוֹלָם וָעֶד. צוּר חַיֵּינוּ מָגֵן יִשְׁעֵנוּ אַתָּה הוּא לְדוֹר וָדוֹר. נוֹדֶה לְךָ וּנְסַפֵּר תְּהִלָּתֶךָ עַל חַיֵּינוּ הַמְּסוּרִים בְּיָדֶךָ וְעַל נִשְׁמוֹתֵינוּ הַפְּקוּדוֹת לָךְ וְעַל נִסֶּיךָ שֶׁבְּכָל יוֹם עִמָּנוּ וְעַל נִפְלְאוֹתֶיךָ וְטוֹבוֹתֶיךָ שֶׁבְּכָל־עֵת עֶרֶב וָבֹקֶר וְצָהֳרָיִם. הַטּוֹב כִּי לֹא־כָלוּ רַחֲמֶיךָ וְהַמְרַחֵם כִּי לֹא־תַמּוּ חֲסָדֶיךָ מֵעוֹלָם קִוִּינוּ לָךְ:

blocks.text: 145 Musaph for the New Year 145
While the Kohanim make their way to the דוכן, the congregation say: ותערב

May our entreaty be pleasing to Thee like the whole-offering and the sacrifice. O Merciful One, restore Thy presence to Zion in Thy great mercies and the order of worship to Jerusalem. Let our eyes behold Thy return to Zion in compassion and let us serve Thee there in awe as in olden times and former years. Blessed art Thou, O Lord, whom alone we wish to worship in awe.
uncertainties: 'whole-offering' is broken at a line end but is a real compound word. 'pres-ence' is a line-break hyphen and was joined.
'Blessed art Thou…' starts a new paragraph after the cue word ברוך.

blocks.text: We thank Thee for Thou art the Lord our God and the God of our fathers for ever and ever. The Rock of our life, the Shield of our salvation art Thou from generation to generation. We thank Thee and tell of Thy fame for our life that is delivered in Thy hand for our souls that are entrusted to Thee and for Thy miracles that are daily with us and for Thy wonders and benefits at all times, evening, morning and noon. O Thou who art good for Thy mercies never end, O Thou who showest mercy for Thy sindnesses never cease, ever have we trusted in Thee.
uncertainties: 'sindnesses' is kept as printed. See source_sic_corr.

blocks.text: We thank Thee because Thou art the Lord our God and the God of our fathers, the God of all flesh, our Creator, the Creator of the beginning. Blessings and thanks to Thy Great and Holy Name for having kept us alive and let us survive. So mayest Thou further keep us alive and let us survive and gather our exiles to the court-yards of Thy Sanctuary in order to observe Thy statutes and do Thy will and serve Thee whole-heartedly; wherefore we thank Thee. Blessed be God to whom thanks are due.
uncertainties: 'Cre-ator', 'may-est' and 'Bless-ed' are line-break hyphens and were joined. 'court-yards' and 'whole-heartedly' fall mid-line, so their hyphens are real.

blocks.text: For all of them may Thy Name, O our King, be continually blessed and exalted for ever and ever. And inscribe for a good life all the children of Thy Covenant. And all the living thank Thee, Selah, and praise Thy Name in truth, O God of our salvation and of our aid, Selah! Blessed art Thou, O Lord, All-benevolent, whose name is goodness and unto whom it is becoming to give thanks.

Our God and God of our fathers, bless us with the threefold blessing that is written in the Torah through Moses Thy servant and was uttered by the mouth of Aaron and his sons the priests, Thy holy people, as it is said:
